data.cultural_impact: Veerangana is an evocative name that resonates with bravery and strength in Hindu culture. It is reminiscent of the fierce warrior princesses and gods in ancient Indian literature, who are revered for their courage and protection of their people. The name Veerangana continues to inspire and empower women, as well as men, to be brave and fearless in the face of challenges. It is also a name that evokes a sense of honor and respect, as it reminds us of the sacrifices made by brave warriors in defense of their land and people.

historical_references.reference: Veerangana was a legendary warrior queen who ruled the Chalukya kingdom in the Deccan region of India during the 11th century. She is best known for her victories against the Chola dynasty and the Western Chalukyas.

Another popular legend about Veerangana describes her as a Jain princess who defied her father's wishes to marry a non-Jain prince and instead chose to live as a warrior. She is said to have led an army of women and fought bravely in various battles during the 12th century.
